entities.evidence: The kings had served Chedorlaomer for twelve years. Genesis 14:1 identifies him as king of Elam.

analysis.evidence: שְׁתֵּים supplies the ‘two’ in שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה ‘twelve years’, the length of time they served Chedorlaomer.
analysis.morphology: Feminine dual absolute cardinal numeral, agreeing with שָׁנָה ‘year’.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה, שְׁתֵּים supplies two and עֶשְׂרֵה supplies ten. Together they count the twelve years of service to Chedorlaomer.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral, the second element of the compound numeral שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה.
analysis.sense: ten, in the numbers eleven to nineteen

analysis.evidence: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה answers how long the kings served Chedorlaomer (עָבְדוּ אֶת כְּדָרְלָעֹמֶר). Their service lasted twelve years.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with no prefix or suffix. The singular form follows the numeral שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה (twelve).
analysis.sense: year, the round of the seasons

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks כְּדָרְלָעֹמֶר as the king they served. Their twelve years of service ended when מָרָדוּ, “they rebelled,” in the thirteenth year. This identifies the service as political subjection.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with the verbal ending ־וּ.
analysis.sense: serve a king as a vassal

analysis.evidence: In עָבְדוּ אֶת כְּדָרְלָעֹמֶר, “they served Chedorlaomer,” אֶת marks the proper name כְּדָרְלָעֹמֶר as the definite direct object of עָבְדוּ.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article with the Hebrew root left unassigned.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:1 identifies Chedorlaomer by the title מֶלֶךְ עֵילָם, “king of Elam.”

analysis.evidence: עָבְדוּ אֶת כְּדָרְלָעֹמֶר means “they served Chedorlaomer.” The name identifies the ruler they served for twelve years, introduced in Genesis 14:1 as king of Elam.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The direct-object marker אֶת is a separate word.
analysis.sense: The personal name of the king of Elam.

analysis.evidence: After twelve years of service, וּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה identifies the thirteenth year as the year of rebellion. The marked word contributes “and” and the “three” in “thirteen.”
analysis.morphology: וּ is the conjunction “and.” שְׁלֹשׁ is a feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral. It combines with עֶשְׂרֵה to count the feminine noun שָׁנָה.

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה, שְׁלֹשׁ supplies ‘three’ and the marked עֶשְׂרֵה supplies ‘-teen’. Together they form ‘thirteen’ and modify the feminine noun שָׁנָה ‘year’.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral, the second element of a compound numeral.
analysis.sense: ten, in the numbers eleven to nineteen

analysis.evidence: After twelve years of service to Chedorlaomer, the kings rebelled. The phrase וּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה places מָרָדוּ, “they rebelled,” in the thirteenth year.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: year, the round of the seasons

draft.change: Add a root article for מרד with the Qal verb מָרַד and its sense of rebelling against a ruler.
draft.definition: To rebel against a ruler by withdrawing allegiance.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:4 sets מָרָדוּ in the thirteenth year against twelve years of service to Chedorlaomer.

analysis.evidence: Both עָבְדוּ and מָרָדוּ have the same plural subject. The kings served Chedorlaomer for twelve years, then rebelled in the thirteenth. Their earlier service identifies the ruler whose authority they rejected.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew Qal perfect, third person common plural. The ending וּ marks the plural subject of the verb.
analysis.sense: To rebel against a ruler to whom one has been subject.
